What is Linux?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerWhy distributions differTry before replacing your systemBefore installationLearning the basicsFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

Linux is the kernel at the center of many operating systems. A Linux distribution, such as Ubuntu, combines that kernel with system tools, applications, and an installer.

Why distributions differ

Distributions choose different desktop interfaces, software packages, release schedules, and support policies. The kernel is only one part of the experience. Choose a distribution with documentation that matches your needs.

Try before replacing your system

Some distributions offer a live USB environment that lets you try the desktop without installing it. Creating that USB erases the selected USB drive. Carefully check the destination and follow the distribution’s official instructions.

Before installation

Back up your files and confirm that you can restore them. Save disk-encryption recovery keys and check hardware compatibility. Installer options that erase or repartition a disk can destroy existing data. Follow the current official guide for the specific release instead of guessing.

Learning the basics

Start with the graphical settings and software manager. Learn how updates work and where your personal files live. Do not run unfamiliar terminal commands with administrator privileges just because a forum post suggests them.
